subject: Post-call: legal & procurement routing — stakeholders + NDA/MSA/DPA next steps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: legal & procurement routing — stakeholders + NDA/MSA/DPA next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on scope and performance expectations. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get contracting moving: 

Recap (from our discovery)
- Primary use case: customer support triage + summary (latency SLOs, redaction/PII controls).
- Expected monthly token volume: small POC (~5–10M tokens/month) then scale.
- Decision criteria: security posture (DPA/SOC2), price per token, predictable latency.

Stakeholder mapping (please confirm):
- Economic buyer: Tom Barton (CPO) — signs final PO/commitment
- Security/legal reviewer: Maria Gomez (security) — technical/security questionnaire, DPA discussions
- Procurement / contracting: Jared Klein — PO process, payment terms
- Technical owner: Sarah Lee — POC coordination and acceptance criteria

Contract routing + ask
- Can you confirm who owns the NDA, MSA, and DPA routing on your side? We typically:
  1) Exchange/sign NDA (DocuSign) to allow redline sharing
  2) Share clean MSA for redlines (legal)
  3) Follow with DPA and any additional security questionnaire

Typical Redwood target turn-times (for planning):
- NDA (DocuSign/simple signature): 1–3 business days
- MSA initial redline turn: 3–7 business days (depends on complexity)
- DPA review: 3–5 business days

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_clean_v2.docx (attached) — this is the clean MSA we’d like to start redlines from.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Sarah/Tom: confirm the owners above and who we should route NDA to (we can send DocuSign).
2) If okay, we’ll send NDA via DocuSign today and follow with the MSA clean copy for redlines.
3) Rishi (legal) from our side will take the MSA redline first; Hannah will coordinate procurement questions.

If you prefer a different sequencing (e.g., MSA first then NDA) we can adapt.

Thanks — aiming to keep contracting on a 2–3 week cadence for a small POC.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Tom / Marissa,

Thanks for the note and the signed NDA — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few items from legal on sequencing and expected turn-times so everyone can plan: 

Preferred sequencing (our recommendation):
1) NDA (done) — good to have this in place.
2) MSA redline exchange: we typically share a clean MSA and accept redlines; we can do an initial pass on counterpart redlines in ~3–5 business days depending on complexity.
3) DPA review: following MSA redlines we’ll address DPA specifics; target 2–4 business days for an initial pass.

If Acme prefers MSA redline first (instead of DPA) that aligns with our process. We can also accept serialized redlines (MSA then DPA) to keep things moving.

Turn-times (our baseline):
- Initial MSA redline turnaround (from Redwood legal): ~4 business days
- Counterparty redline review (Acme legal): variable — please advise typical internal turn-times
- DPA review: ~3 business days after we have MSA alignment

I’ve attached the clean MSA we referenced. Marissa / Hannah — happy to lead the MSA redline once we get confirmation of the Acme redline sequencing. Sarah / Tom — please confirm who on your legal side will be handling MSA redlines and the best email to send the editable copy to.

Regards,
